# X6 R276 — exact support-label bit projection and strict fifth-pencil frontier

P000 V5 and ACTIVE worldview, joint relation preservation and residual fidelity retained. Auxiliary BRC weight coefficient algebra only, not native spatial plane or time dynamics.

## Frozen inputs and scope
R247@7e54892a45579bdc497c27e061399339d1fb3512 (fdbef2ee6e6c32573f3a1ccd171cb5337de520fa), R275@001076e59298e45715cb58c87ab3395c53d005a8 (9732c23573cf3071a782d0b84d511494ebb1c745), same Port 10, 1935 directions, six-pair joint BRC, weights (17t,B,22t,D), 47 support labels, 51 endpoints, 98 germs, 2225 linear partitions. Capacity exclusions inherit R247 necessary-wall and complete pure-linear suffix premises. Only c=1 strict endpoint words on five pencils; no zero-word or full root closure claim.

## Lossless support-label count projection
Each support tag in R247 is a disjoint contiguous block of two or four germ bits (verified programmatically). Let F be the mask of the first bit of every block, H the mask of first bits of four-bit blocks. For any 98-bit germ mask s, put v=s OR (s>>1), W=(v OR ((v>>2) AND H)) AND F. At a two-bit block start j, W_j=s_j OR s_(j+1); at a four-bit block start it is OR of all four germ bits. No other bits survive. Thus popcount(W) equals exactly the number of support tags intersecting s for every s; no loss of capacity-count information. The original germ mask s is retained for all partition intersections and recursive decisions, so this is only a count-observer optimization, not a replacement for joint branch state. It does not assert any time-dependent/native reduction. Implement popcount using 32-bit SWAR on four disjoint words; exact integer arithmetic (multiply intermediate <2^53) and BigInt shifts. Cross-check on 98 deterministic two-bit masks and all 2225 linear partition pairs and unions. A separate 10,000,000-check run reproduced R275's four prefix stages and reached fifth visit 18259; that is a check of compatibility, not added novelty.

## Actual run and frontier
The four-line prefix had to be reconstructed because R275 retained only three sample survivors, not the full word bank. Repeat work is not counted as scientific increment. Below is the actual single 65,000,000-ceiling run; cutoff null means all five stages complete. In a cutoff run the final visited word may be interrupted: exclude only explicitly classified words. All survivors are necessary-condition survivors, not correct trees. The entire survivor bank is serialized rather than just examples.

```json
{"groups":[[18,2,0,36],[6,5,43],[48,21,29,23,46],[4,14,16,12,3,8],[26,19,34,20,25,28,39,1,37]],"hist":[{"patterns":11,"visits":11,"direct":0,"alg":0,"recursive":0,"surv":11,"checks":204},{"patterns":7,"visits":77,"direct":0,"alg":0,"recursive":0,"surv":77,"checks":2676},{"patterns":16,"visits":1232,"direct":8,"alg":180,"recursive":44,"surv":1000,"checks":319851},{"patterns":22,"visits":22000,"direct":5086,"alg":10764,"recursive":1099,"surv":5051,"checks":3439695},{"patterns":46,"visits":232346,"direct":103217,"alg":102481,"recursive":18195,"surv":8453,"checks":39153099}],"checks":42915525,"cut":null,"bankPrefixes":2243,"survivors":8453,"firstMask":"1555555555555554555554555","quadMask":"400000400"}
```

Each bank line encodes four local pattern indices (alphabet 0-9,A-Z,a-z; index 0=all positive, other indices in R275 l-major then h-major order) and a hexadecimal bitmask of permitted fifth pattern indices. It preserves distinct endpoint words even when branch masks coincide. Decode using R275 patterns(k), reconstruct ps, a,b,R and extendCircuit for k=0..4; no repeat of the completed fifth-prefix decisions is necessary for these survivors. If cutoff nonnull the unfinished visits require separate completion, starting at the interrupted visit. The four-line bank ordering is exactly R275 deterministic expansion.

## Reproduction
Extract the first JavaScript blocks from pinned R247 and R275. Replace the original R247 count declaration/function (from const cc=new Map() through the end of count) with:

```javascript
const cc=new Map();let firstMask=0n,quadMask=0n;for(let t of tag){let l=t&-t;if(t===3n*l)firstMask|=l;else if(t===15n*l){firstMask|=l;quadMask|=l;}else throw Error("noncontiguous tag");}function pc32(x){x=x-((x>>>1)&0x55555555);x=(x&0x33333333)+((x>>>2)&0x33333333);return (((x+(x>>>4))&0x0f0f0f0f)*0x01010101)>>>24;}function count(s){let v=s|(s>>1n);v=(v|((v>>2n)&quadMask))&firstMask;return pc32(Number(v&0xffffffffn))+pc32(Number((v>>32n)&0xffffffffn))+pc32(Number((v>>64n)&0xffffffffn))+pc32(Number(v>>96n));}for(let i=0;i<98;i++){let s=(1n<<BigInt(i))|((1n<<BigInt((i*37+5)%98)));if(count(s)!==tag.filter(t=>t&s).length)throw Error("count test");}for(let [a,b] of Q)for(let s of [a,b,a|b])if(count(s)!==tag.filter(t=>t&s).length)throw Error("count bank test");
```

Use R275's patch with ceiling=65000000 and replace its terminal return with:

```javascript
const alphabet="0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz";
function wordID(p,k){let [l,h]=p.word,n=groups[k].length;return l>h?0:1+l*n-l*(l-1)/2+h-l}
let bank=new Map();for(let st of states){let key=st.ps.slice(0,4).map((p,k)=>alphabet[wordID(p,k)]).join("");let bit=1n<<BigInt(wordID(st.ps[4],4));bank.set(key,(bank.get(key)||0n)|bit)}
return {groups,hist,checks,cut,bank:[...bank].map(([k,v])=>k+":"+v.toString(16)).join("\n"),bankPrefixes:bank.size,survivors:states.length,firstMask:firstMask.toString(16),quadMask:quadMask.toString(16)};
```
